ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Meal timing and pump activation

A patient takes a delayed-release PPI inconsistently after a large evening meal and has poor symptom control. The clinician reviews adherence and recommends taking the scheduled dose before a meal. Which principle supports that instruction?

  1. The drug requires bacterial fermentation after eating
  2. Acid secretion must be completely absent for activation
  3. Meals prevent all systemic absorption
  4. Drug availability should coincide with meal-activated proton pumps
  5. Food must chemically neutralize the drug
Answer and explanation

Drug availability should coincide with meal-activated proton pumps

Many PPIs work best when taken before meals so active drug encounters stimulated pumps; formulation-specific instructions still apply.

Option explanations

Drug availability should coincide with meal-activated proton pumps: Many PPIs work best when taken before meals so active drug encounters stimulated pumps; formulation-specific instructions still apply.

Food must chemically neutralize the drug: Food does not serve to neutralize the drug.

The drug requires bacterial fermentation after eating: Bacterial fermentation is not required.

Acid secretion must be completely absent for activation: Acidic canaliculi contribute to activation.

Meals prevent all systemic absorption: Meals do not universally eliminate absorption.
